description: DCGVR (DEF CON Groups Virtual Reality) Village at DEF CON 30 connects global hacker groups with community presentations on cloud exploitation, hardware security, packet analysis, and social engineering.

talks.title: DCGVR Village Keynote
talks.teaser: Jayson E. Street delivers the DCGVR Village keynote, reflecting on global DEF CON Groups, community resilience, and unconventional security career paths.

talks.title: Attack Trends in 2022
talks.teaser: An analysis of prominent cyberattack vectors, adversary tradecraft shifts, and ransomware trends observed across 2022.

talks.title: Exploits & Dragons: Gamifying Infosec Education with Tabletop RPGs
talks.teaser: Exploits & Dragons explores how tabletop roleplaying game mechanics can be used to simulate cyber attacks, incident response, and threat modeling.

talks.title: How to Start & Run a DEF CON Group (DCG)
talks.teaser: A practical guide to founding, organizing, and sustaining local DEF CON Groups (DCGs) to foster community learning and technical collaboration.

talks.title: Advanced Packet Wrangling with tcpdump
talks.teaser: Mastering advanced tcpdump command-line syntax, Berkeley Packet Filters (BPF), and real-time packet carving for network troubleshooting and threat analysis.

talks.title: Ham Radio is Not Just for Dinosaurs
talks.teaser: Demystifying amateur radio for modern hackers, exploring digital packet radio, APRS telemetry, SDR integration, and emergency communications.

talks.title: How My High School Creative Writing Class Prepared Me for Social Engineering
talks.teaser: Exploring how storytelling, character development, and narrative pacing learned in creative writing form the foundation of compelling social engineering pretexts.

talks.title: Fun with Bookmarks: Weaponizing Bookmarklets & Browser Storage
talks.teaser: Exploring the offensive and productivity utility of browser bookmarklets, demonstrating client-side automation, DOM manipulation, and security auditing tools.

talks.title: Careful Who You Colab With: Security Risks in Google Colab & Shared Notebooks
talks.teaser: Auditing security boundaries in Google Colaboratory, demonstrating data exfiltration vectors, runtime sandbox escapes, and risks in shared machine learning notebooks.

talks.title: How Getting a Free Phone Got Me to Report Critical Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: The journey of reverse engineering a budget Android smartphone, uncovering pre-installed carrier bloatware vulnerabilities and navigating responsible disclosure.

talks.title: Security Concerns of the Medical Laboratory
talks.teaser: An inside look at vulnerabilities in clinical laboratory automation, analyzing unauthenticated analyzer instruments, legacy LIMS software, and patient data risks.

talks.title: AWS Metadata Privilege Escalation: Exploiting IMDSv1 & IAM Roles
talks.teaser: Deconstructing AWS Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) exploitation, abusing SSRF to harvest temporary IAM credentials and escalate cloud permissions.

talks.title: Glitter Nail Polish vs. The Evil Maid: Low-Cost Tamper Evident Verification
talks.teaser: Using unique optical patterns of glitter nail polish to create uncloneable, low-cost physical tamper-evident seals against Evil Maid attacks on laptops and screws.

talks.title: When Firefox Gets Angry: Fuzzing & Exploiting Gecko Engine Internals
talks.teaser: Dissecting the internals of Mozilla Firefox's Gecko rendering engine, exploring DOM fuzzing methodologies and memory corruption vulnerability classes.
